input.summary: Seven industry-standard patterns are mapped; six are active but all are blocked by foundational evidence gaps.
covers: Governed data foundation for AI / LLM automation pattern
Payment integrity and leakage reduction pattern

story.meaning: Meridian has correctly identified seven high-value industry patterns, but every one is blocked by the same foundational deficits: no certified medallion architecture, no patient/member identity spine, no formal governance operating model, and no AI audit trail.
story.observed: Six of seven patterns are active-status with high confidence. The seventh — end-to-end cost transparency — sits at candidate grade, held back by ungoverned provider contract terms and unproven claims/GL calendar alignment.
story.matters: Without closing the lakehouse foundation and governance gaps first, none of the seven patterns can advance from planning to decision grade. The patterns are strategically correct; the platform readiness is not.
story.supports: Nexus maps each pattern to its specific evidence gate, surfacing exactly which foundation gaps must close before investment decisions can be made with confidence.

findings: All seven industry patterns are strategically aligned to Meridian's stated CEO, CFO, and CDAO priorities — but zero patterns have cleared their evidence gate for decision-grade advancement.
The unified clinical + claims lakehouse is the prerequisite platform for four of the remaining six patterns; its foundation gaps create a cascade risk across the entire portfolio.

Payment integrity and call center optimization are the two patterns most likely to yield near-term value, yet both are blocked by ungoverned source assets — SAS model lineage and contact center transcripts respectively.

Provider quality and end-to-end cost transparency share a single critical blocker: provider contract terms are not in governed digital form, making both patterns dependent on the same remediation action.

breakdown.title: Industry Pattern Readiness — Meridian Health System

rows.label: Unified Clinical + Claims Lakehouse
rows.note: Medallion architecture, identity spine, and AWS/Databricks foundation not evidenced

rows.label: Governed Data Foundation for AI / LLM
rows.note: No governance operating model, no semantic layer, no AI audit trail

rows.label: Payment Integrity & Leakage Reduction
rows.note: SAS model lineage ungoverned; provider entity resolution unproven

rows.label: Call Center Optimization
rows.note: Transcript governance, real-time CRM integration, and intent taxonomy not certified

rows.label: End-to-End Cost Transparency
rows.note: Provider contract terms not in governed digital form; lowest readiness of the seven

chain: Industry patterns → Lakehouse foundation (prerequisite for 4 of 7 patterns)
Lakehouse foundation → Governance operating model (prerequisite for all AI/LLM patterns)
Governance operating model → Semantic layer + AI audit trail (prerequisite for decision-grade advancement)
Provider contract digitization → Cost transparency + Provider quality (shared single blocker)
SAS model lineage → Payment integrity (current detection platform, ungoverned)
relationships.note: The seven patterns form a dependency stack, not a parallel portfolio. Lakehouse foundation and governance operating model are the two load-bearing prerequisites; failure to close either blocks the majority of Meridian's stated strategic priorities simultaneously.

gaps.missing: No certified medallion architecture on AWS/Databricks
gaps.blocks: Unified clinical + claims lakehouse — the foundational pattern for four downstream use cases
gaps.needed: Certified Bronze/Silver/Gold layer design with Epic Clarity, claims, and pharmacy sources loaded
gaps.handoff: Platform/Architecture team must certify medallion design before data team can begin identity spine work

gaps.missing: No formal data governance operating model
gaps.blocks: All seven patterns — particularly AI/LLM automation where audit trail and data quality rules are also absent
gaps.needed: Governance charter, data steward assignments, semantic layer ownership, and data quality rule registry
gaps.handoff: CDAO office must stand up governance operating model before any AI/LLM pattern can advance

gaps.missing: Provider contract terms not in governed digital form
gaps.blocks: End-to-end cost transparency (candidate) and provider quality and performance (active)
gaps.needed: Digitized, governed contract terms with attribution ownership certified
gaps.handoff: Network Contracting and Finance must co-own contract digitization; CDAO certifies governance

gaps.missing: SAS payment integrity model lineage ungoverned; provider entity resolution unproven
gaps.blocks: Payment integrity and leakage reduction pattern — prevents leakage quantification
gaps.needed: Governed model lineage, provider entity resolution, investigation workflow, and recovery tracking evidence
gaps.handoff: Health Plan Ops and Analytics must document SAS model lineage before migration or augmentation decisions

gaps.missing: Contact center transcript governance, intent taxonomy, and member identity linkage not certified
gaps.blocks: Call center optimization — agent-assist and next-best-action cannot advance
gaps.needed: Transcript governance policy, certified intent taxonomy, real-time CRM integration proof, member identity linkage
gaps.handoff: Chief Experience Officer and CIO must jointly certify transcript governance before analytics build begins

evidence.name: Unified Clinical + Claims Lakehouse Pattern
evidence.facts: Pattern is active and high-confidence but blocked by four foundational gaps: no medallion architecture, no identity spine, no claims/pharmacy harmonization, and AWS/Databricks foundation not ready.
evidence.missing: Certified medallion architecture; patient/member identity spine; claims and pharmacy harmonization proof

evidence.name: Governed Data Foundation for AI / LLM Automation Pattern
evidence.facts: Flagged as top priority by CEO, CFO, CIO, and CDAO. Blocked by absence of formal governance operating model, certified semantic layer, AI audit trail, and data quality rules.
evidence.missing: Governance operating model; semantic layer certification; AI audit trail; data quality rule registry

evidence.name: Call Center Optimization Pattern
evidence.facts: Contact center platform and CRM are current-core systems but ungoverned for analytics. Transcript governance, real-time integration, intent taxonomy, and member identity linkage are all unproven.
evidence.missing: Transcript governance policy; certified intent taxonomy; real-time CRM integration; member identity linkage

evidence.name: Payment Integrity and Leakage Reduction Pattern
evidence.facts: SAS estate is the current detection platform. Model lineage is ungoverned. Provider entity resolution and recovery tracking workflows are not yet evidenced, preventing leakage quantification.
evidence.missing: SAS model lineage governance; provider entity resolution; investigation and recovery workflow evidence

evidence.name: End-to-End Cost Transparency Pattern
evidence.facts: Only candidate-status pattern in the set. Provider contract terms not in governed digital form is the single largest blocker. Claims/GL calendar alignment and cost allocation rules also unproven.
evidence.missing: Provider contract digitization; claims/GL calendar alignment; cost allocation rules; margin semantic model

evidence.name: Provider Quality, Performance & Automated Close Patterns
evidence.rows: 2 of 7 (active — provider quality medium confidence; automated close high confidence)
evidence.facts: Provider quality shares the contract digitization blocker with cost transparency. Automated close and reporting is high-confidence active but depends on the same governance and semantic layer foundations.
evidence.missing: Attribution ownership certification for provider quality; GL/close automation baseline for automated reporting
